elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: New Section 5.5 grants the Company only a licence ("HDI hereby grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables and work product"); no operative sentence vests ownership of deliverables or work product in the Company.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered text; Section 5.5 is a licence grant only. To meet this element the drafter would need an express "HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in the Deliverables and work product".

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 says only "HDI shall retain ownership of its generic tools and know-how"; there is no express retention of HDI's pre-existing intellectual property, which is a broader and different category.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables and work product developed for the Company" — the grant runs to the deliverables as a whole, including HDI IP embedded in them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" in Section 5.5 covers the Site and all other deliverables and work product.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables and work product" in Section 5.5.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 restricts HDI's use of "Content, user information, data or other materials belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company" but contains no affirmative statement that the Company retains all right, title and interest in that data; Section 8.1 treats it only as Confidential Information.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license or right of HDI in Content, user information, data or other materials belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company is limited to processing the same solely to provide the services under this Agreement." The trigger covers every category belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company, not selected data types, and no broader exploitation right is retained elsewhere.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No express no-joint-ownership sentence was added; the insertion is silent on joint ownership. (No retained clause creates joint ownership either, but the preferred checklist requires the express negation.)

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5, first sentence: "HDI shall retain ownership of its generic tools and know-how."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "HDI hereby grants the Company a perpetual ... license" covering "the Site and any other deliverables and work product developed for the Company under this Agreement".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" in Section 5.5.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears in the express string of licence modifiers in Section 5.5.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense" in Section 5.5.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the Site and any other deliverables and work product developed for the Company under this Agreement for its business" — use and modify rights are express and business-scoped.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The same grant expressly includes "sublicense ... for its business"; no retained clause restricts sublicensing (Section 5.2 concerns artistic/editorial control and approval only).

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Third sentence of Section 5.5 limits "[a]ny license or right of HDI" in Company Content, user information, data or other materials to "processing the same solely to provide the services under this Agreement"; no distribution, resale or broader "purposes contemplated" right survives.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the inserted Section 5.5 delivers all eight fallback elements in operative language — HDI's retention of generic tools and know-how, a perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and all other deliverables and work product for the Company's business, and a data-use limitation confined to processing solely to provide the services.

Preferred level is not complete and the drafter should not claim it: there is no Company ownership statement, no assignment of deliverables from HDI, no express retention of HDI's pre-existing IP (only generic tools and know-how), no statement that the Company retains all rights in its data, and no no-joint-ownership sentence.

The data-limitation sentence uses a category trigger ("belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company") rather than selected named data types, so it does not fail the Customer-Data scope test; it also imposes no standing HDI exploitation right.

Minimality holds: the finding is a genuine gap (no IP/licence clause existed), the fix is a single concise inserted section, nothing outside the checklist was deleted or paraphrased, and no survival tail, expense allocation, indemnity or procedural extras were added. Reciting "the Site and any other deliverables and work product" is necessary because the Agreement defines no "Deliverables" term.

Intent is preserved: Section 5.2 (artistic/editorial control, written acceptance, consent to publish), the General Manager provision and Section 8.1 confidentiality survive unchanged and do not contradict the new licence; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created ("services" ties to the Services performed under the Agreement, and "Content" is used as elsewhere in the Agreement).

Optional strengthening (rationale-level only, not a defect at the fallback): add "The Company retains all right, title and interest in its Content, user information and data" and "No intellectual property shall be jointly owned" if the counterparty will accept the preferred position.
